newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: BULLIMORE'S WIFE WOULD SAY YES TO NEW VOYAGE
The wife of rescued British sailor, Tony Bullimore, says she won't try to stop her husband competing in another round-the-world yacht race.
Mr Bullimore is recovering from frostbite and a partially severed finger which he suffered while in the hull of his capsized yacht in the Southern Ocean.
The 57-year-old made a triumphant return to Fremantle yesterday after being rescued, along with a fellow competitor, Thierry Dubois, by the combined efforts of the Australian Navy and Air Force.
Lalel Bullimore had an emotional reunion with her husband after flying out from England and says although not happy at the prospect, she wouldn't stand in his way.
MOVE TO ELIMINATE GUN LOOPHOLE
The Federal Government is trying to remove a loophole which means some gun owners can keep semi-automatic weapons that are banned under State and Territory laws.
Regulations under the Defence Act mean some gun club owners can keep semi-automatic weapons.
A spokesman for Defence Minister, Ian McLachlan, says the regulations were made in 1903 and are obsolete.
He says negotiations have been under way to repeal the regulations since Police Ministers agreed last year about new tougher gun laws.
He says when the regulations are repealed, gun club members won't be able to own any weapons that they can't be licenced for under State laws.
IN TENNIS...
In the Australian Open....Jennifer Capriati has gone down to Jolene Watanabe, 6-2, 3-6, 6-4 at Melbourne Park.
Meanwhile another Australian is through to the second round, with Peter Tramacchi victorious over Belgium's Johan Van Hairck.
Tramacchi fought back after losing the first set to win the next two, 6-3, 6-4, before his opponent retired hurt in the fourth....Tramacchi was up 3-2 at the time.
Meanwhile, 15-year-old Australian qualifier, Lleyton Hewitt, has lost to Spain's Sergi Bruguera, 6-3, 6-4, 6-3.
And, another Spaniard, Alberto Berasategio has beaten Australia's Todd Larkham, 6-1, 6-2, 6-4.
PULP FICTION MAY HAVE INSPIRED ROBBERIES
Perth police say a string of armed robberies at restaurants may be inspired by the restaurant robbery scene in the film, Pulp Fiction.
Assistant Commissioner, Bob Kucera, says about six restaurants have been held-up during the past couple of months, and patrons were also robbed.
Assistant Commissioner Kucera says there's been a swing towards the use of violence in the robberies, which is a new phenomenon.
He fears they may be linked with the cult film.
Police say a major crackdown on armed robberies will start tonight, with special groups set up throughout the metropolitan area to concentrate solely on armed hold-ups.
VETERANS DISCRIMINATION HEARINGS UNDERWAY
The Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission has begun hearing claims of sexual discrimination against war veterans and a war widow.
One of the cases involves discrepancies in eligibility for war service pensions, with women qualifying at 55 and men only at 60.
Two World War Two veterans are demanding the Repatriation Commission give them the same free health services available to ex-service women.
And - John Sinclair says his wife, Dorothy, is alleging she was discriminated against when her war widow pension ended with her second marriage in 1981.
UNION SAYS BANK TO CONSULT BEFORE REDUNDANCIES
The Finance Sector Union says it has a joint agreement with the St George bank not to cut jobs without consultation.
Yesterday's vote by shareholders to clear the way for the banks to merge has left workers unsure of their future.
Both banks have signalled the merger will mean around 170 branch closures and job losses, with some estimates putting job cuts at one thousand.
Both the union and the St George are hopeful of meeting the job cuts through voluntary redundancies.
The Union says today's meeting with representatives from the St George and Advance banks, didn't reveal any figures for redundancies.
REIFFEL REJOINS OZ LINE UP
Victorian pace bowler Paul Reiffel is one of two changes to the Australian cricket team for Thursday's one-day international against Pakistan.
Reiffel, who dropped out of the team with a hamstring injury, passed a fitness test this morning, and joins new boy Darren Lehmann in the team.
Mark Waugh is out injured, and Tom Moody has been dropped.
Reiffel says while Australia can't qualify for the World Series Cup finals, they will be going all-out for victory.
